sections.title: About me
sections.body:
Graduate student at the University of Vermont studying Electrical Engineering. I grew an affinity towards electronics which drew me into the field that I am in now, complimented by my curiosity about how the universe worked on the macro and micro scale. I now work on the analysis of power transistors smaller than specks of dust with the goal of optimizing them for many industries, including space exploration.

Outside of my academic life, I play and write music in my free time and love to ski and bike. On this website, I hope to include my academic achievements as well as my personal life.

sections.title: Motivation
sections.body:
Currently, I am studying the reliability of high voltage GaN bidirectional HEMTs using devices which are already manufactured. I am exploring topics like stress effects of hot carrier injection and time dependent dielectric breakdown. The exploration of this topic is directly relevant to many applications and industries, such as: 

- Automotive: Near-zero failure rates, meaning reliability is imperative.
- Data center and AI server PSUs: Reliable bidirectional switches mitigate thermal stress and improve efficiency.
- AC-AC converters: Single switch blocking both polarities every cycle replaces two devices. Can only be done once reliability is studied.
- Space and lunar power (Artemis): In space, repairs are not possible, temperature range is extreme and less parts means less weight goes to space. Studying the reliability yields space programs with knowledge on how best to implement these devices.
- Consumer batteries and electronics: Compact bidirectional switches cuts losses and saves space on board in phones, laptops and tools.

I am aim to complete and defend my thesis by December 2027 on my study of the reliability of GaN bidirectional HEMTs.

projects.title: Reliability of Bidirectional GaN (Thesis Topic)
projects.summary: Study on the stress effects of hot carrier injection, time dependent dielectric breakdown and gate length in GaN bidirectional switches
projects.body:
## Overview

GaN devices have many properties which excel in areas of radio frequency and power. Specifically with power devices, these devices can operate at very high voltages. When a high voltage is applied to the device, aside from the intended current flow in the 2DEG, there is a strong vertical electric field which can drive hot electrons into the substrate and buffer layers, trapping them at various points. This hot carrier injection is a phenomenon which accelerates the degradation and wears-out of devices. A second, independent wear-out mechanism occurs at the gate called time dependent dielectric breakdown. As the electric field across the device is active, defects can slowly generate, eventually forming a conductive path which breaks the device down. 

![GaNBDSHCITDDB](images/ganbdshcitddb-mw15a55p.png)

In my research, I explore both of these topics to know more about them and to help engineers implement these devices in extreme conditions like rapid switching in automotive or extreme temperatures in space.

I am working in collaboration with the V-GaN Tech Hub to complete my measurements and will focus on varying the dual-gate lengths, and stress conditions like $V_{GS}, V_{GB}$ and $T$. I am measuring the parameters of the device with tests like, IdVg, IdVd, Pulsed IV, CV, Charge Pump and $I_{sub}$. After each parametric measurement, I will equally stress the devices undr the stress conditions and emulate HTGB and HTRB conditions many times. I will study the parametric shift over time with these devices.

Since there are many dimensions I am looking at with stress, I am using a hierarchy based data format file called HDF5. This allows me to sort my data by attributes rather than sifting through by only condition, or location. Since HDF5 normally is interfaced within a terminal setting, I decided to have Claude help build a UI which allows me to click through similar to a file directory, but have the ability to view data points from: testing condition, location of device or size of the gate.


![4D](images/4d-mw15lpoo.png)

To analyze data in this UI, I have implemented many paths to view/import data. You can import data directly into the database in the application and it saves based on the title of the file. I can view all datapoints from a wafer view, a location view or a calculation view. From the calculation view, I can automatically pull the parameters based on the type of curve which saves me all of the time for analysis. This application streamlines the busy work and allows me to focus on writing the thesis and stressing the device more.


![wafermap](images/wafermap-mw15vnj1.png)
